model_description:
Anthropic's most capable widely released model, aimed at demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic
work. Thinking is always on and cannot be disabled; the raw chain of thought is never returned. Forced tool choice
(any/tool) returns a 400, thinking blocks are bound to the producing model, and editing earlier turns invalidates them
("preserved thinking"). Requires 30-day data retention.

Predecessor to Claude Fable 5.1 in the same tier and at the same per-token price, still served. Thinking
is always on; effort is tunable from low through max. Unlike 5.1 it still accepts forced tool choice and does not run the
preserved-thinking history check. Cache reads are priced higher than on 5.1.
Anthropic's fast, low-cost Claude 4.5 model with near-frontier intelligence for high-volume work.

High-speed variant of Opus 4.6, optimized for rapid responses while retaining strong reasoning and capabilities.
Retired: fast mode is no longer offered on Opus 4.6 or 4.7 and is now limited to Claude Opus 5 and Opus 4.8,
which serve it at $10/$50 per million tokens rather than the rates below.
Anthropic's previous-generation Opus model with 1M context, retained for downstream compatibility.
Anthropic's most capable model. Exceptional at complex reasoning, coding, creative collaboration, and scientific analysis.

Opus-tier model preceding Claude Opus 5, with the same request surface as Opus 4.7. Adaptive thinking
must be requested explicitly — omitting the thinking parameter runs without it. Supports fast mode, task budgets, and
mid-conversation system messages.

Anthropic's flagship Opus-tier model. Adaptive thinking is on by default (omitting the thinking parameter
runs it), and effort is tunable from low through max. Supports a 1M-token context window, 128K max output, task budgets,
mid-conversation system messages, and fast mode. budget_tokens and assistant prefill are removed and return a 400.
Points to the latest stable Opus release. Use when you want the newest Claude without pinning a version.
Anthropic's balanced Claude model with strong speed/intelligence tradeoffs, extended thinking, and 1M context.

Anthropic's balanced mid-tier model: Opus-family context and output limits at a lower price. Adaptive
thinking with effort levels low through max, 1M-token context, and 128K max output. Does not support mid-conversation
system messages; budget_tokens and assistant prefill are removed.

Claudinio runs a unified model optimized for coding agents. All plans access the same high-performance model — the
difference is the hourly protection level, tuned for each developer profile.
Mistral's code-specialized model for software engineering and code completion workflows.
Groq-hosted DeepSeek R1 distilled Llama 70B reasoning model.
Fast, efficient DeepSeek variant. Optimized for high-volume applications where latency and cost are critical.
August 2026 snapshot of DeepSeek V4 Pro, priced well below the original V4 Pro release with the same 1M-token context window.
DeepSeek's flagship model. Excellent reasoning and code capabilities at a fraction of OpenAI's cost.

Current DeepSeek Flash-tier model, adding image input over the V4 Flash line. 1M-token context window
with a 384K output limit and an unusually cheap cache-read rate.
Previous-generation Gemini. Good balance of speed, cost, and capability for standard tasks.
Fast, efficient Gemini model. Optimized for high-volume applications with strong reasoning and code performance.
Google's flagship model. Exceptional at long-context tasks, multimodal reasoning, and code generation.
Cheapest current Gemini tier, keeping the full 1M-token context window and multimodal input at a fraction of Flash pricing.
Previous Flash-tier Gemini release, still served. Same context window, output limit, modalities, and pricing as Gemini 3.8 Flash.

Google's current Flash-tier Gemini model. Natively multimodal — text, image, audio, video, and document
input with text output — with a 1M-token context window and 64K max output.
Google's smaller open-weight instruction-tuned model. Efficient for constrained deployment environments.
Google's open-weight instruction-tuned model. Strong reasoning in a smaller footprint. Good for fine-tuning and self-hosting.
Fast open-weight GLM model optimized for multilingual dialogue, tool calling, and reasoning.
Open-weight Z.AI GLM model with strong multilingual, reasoning, and instruction-following capabilities.
Higher-throughput GLM-5 Turbo model for production Z.AI workloads.
Updated GLM-5.1 model with current Z.AI pricing and long-context support.
Z.AI's GLM-5.2 model, the base that GLM-5.3 is post-trained from. Long-context text model aimed at coding and agentic work.

Fast, low-cost variant of GLM-5.3 with the largest context window in the family. Unlike the full GLM-5.3
it accepts image and video input alongside text, at roughly one fifteenth the input cost.

Z.AI's flagship model for complex coding, long-horizon agentic work, and cybersecurity tasks, released
August 2026. Uses the same base model as GLM-5.2 with its capability gains coming from scaled-up post-training. Shipped
via API and the GLM Coding Plan; weights are not publicly available.
Z.AI GLM-5 model for current-generation reasoning and agentic workloads.
Vision-capable GLM-5 Turbo variant for multimodal document, image, and video inputs.
Deprecated 16K GPT-3.5 Turbo snapshot retained for legacy downstream configurations.
Similar capabilities as text-davinci-003 but compatible with legacy Completions endpoint and not Chat Completions.
Most capable GPT-3.5 model and optimized for chat at 1/10th the cost of text-davinci-003.
Same capabilities as the standard gpt-4 mode but with 4x the context length.
Legacy GPT-4 Turbo model with a 128K context window. Kept for integrations that still route older GPT-4 workloads.
Smaller GPT-4.1 variant balancing latency, price, and strong general-purpose capability.
Lowest-cost GPT-4.1 variant for classification, extraction, and latency-sensitive tasks.
Large-context GPT-4.1 model for coding, instruction following, and multimodal document workflows.
GPT-4 successor with improved reasoning and instruction following. Strong all-around model between GPT-4o and GPT-5 series.
More capable than any GPT-3.5 model able to do more complex tasks and optimized for chat.
Smaller, faster, cheaper GPT-4o. Optimized for high-volume, cost-sensitive applications.
GPT-4 Omni — multimodal model with vision, audio, and text. Fast and cost-efficient relative to GPT-4 Turbo.
Lower-cost GPT-5 variant for high-volume tasks that still benefit from reasoning support.
Smallest GPT-5 variant for inexpensive, latency-sensitive automation.
Codex-optimized GPT-5.3 model for coding agents and long-running software engineering tasks.
GPT-5.4 optimized for image understanding and generation. Multimodal model supporting vision tasks.
Fast, cost-efficient GPT-5.4 variant for coding, computer use, and subagent workloads.
Lowest-latency GPT-5.4 variant for inexpensive high-volume tasks.
High-capability GPT-5.4 Pro model for the hardest reasoning and professional workloads.
Current OpenAI model for coding and professional work with a 1M token context window.
Most capable OpenAI model with largest context window. Optimized for complex reasoning, advanced coding, and scientific analysis.
Capable OpenAI model with large context window. Strong for complex tasks at lower cost than Pro.

Smallest and cheapest tier of the GPT-5.6 family, at one tenth Terra's input cost while keeping the full
1.05M-token context window and 128K output limit. Suited to high-volume classification, extraction, and routing.

Top tier of the GPT-5.6 family, superseded as OpenAI's flagship by GPT-6 Astra but still served. Aliased
as gpt-5.6. Accepts text and image input with text output. OpenAI lists promotional pricing available at least through
2026-11-21; the rates here are the standard published rates, and OpenRouter currently bills below them.

Mid tier of the GPT-5.6 family. Same 1.05M-token context window and 128K output limit as Sol at roughly
half the input cost, making it the general-purpose default of the family.
General GPT-5 model for reasoning, coding, and multimodal text/image workflows.

OpenAI's flagship model and the first of the GPT-6 generation, released September 2026. Accepts text and
image input with text output, supports tool calling and the full Responses API tool set, and exposes effort levels from
low through max. Prompts beyond 272K input tokens reprice the entire request — 2x input and cache rates, 1.5x output —
not just the overflow.
Grok 4.20 optimized for multi-agent workflows. Enhanced coordination for parallel task execution.
xAI's flagship model. Strong reasoning with real-time web access. Known for personality and directness.
Long-context Grok release with a 1M-token window and 900K output limit at roughly half the cost of Grok 4.5 and 4.6.
Predecessor to Grok 4.6 with the same context window, output limit, and pricing; cached input is billed slightly lower.

xAI's current flagship Grok model. Trades the very large context window of the Grok 4.20 line for a
500K-token window with a 450K output limit, at a higher per-token price.
Moonshot AI's flagship model. Strong long-context understanding and reasoning at competitive pricing.

Moonshot AI's most capable model, released July 2026. A 2.8-trillion-parameter model built on Kimi Delta
Attention — a hybrid linear attention mechanism — plus Attention Residuals, with native visual understanding and a
1M-token context window. Supports vision input, tool calling, extended reasoning, prompt caching, and structured outputs.
Flat pay-as-you-go pricing with no tiering by context length.
Groq-hosted Llama 3.1 8B model for very low-latency, low-cost chat and automation.
Groq-hosted Llama 3.3 70B model optimized for fast general-purpose chat and tool workloads.
MiniMax M2.1 model with strong multilingual programming and enhanced coding experience.
High-speed MiniMax M2.5 variant for lower-latency coding and agent workloads.
MiniMax M2.5 model for complex programming, agent, and productivity tasks.
High-speed MiniMax M2.7 variant with the same capability profile and faster output for latency-sensitive workloads.
Beginning the journey of recursive self-improvement. Strong for programming, tool calling, search, office productivity, and complex agent workflows.
MiniMax M2 model for agentic workflows, advanced reasoning, function calling, and real-time streaming.

MiniMax-M3 is a multimodal foundation model from MiniMax. It supports text, image, and video inputs with text output, a 1M-token context window, and is suited for
long-horizon agentic work, coding, and tool use. It is built on MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA), which replaces full attention with KV-block selection to cut per-token
compute at long context — roughly 1/20 the cost of the previous generation at 1M tokens, with substantially faster prefill and decode while retaining quality across
most tasks.
Mistral-7B fine-tuned on instruction datasets publicly available on HuggingFace.
Mistral-7B-v0.1 is a small yet powerful model adaptable to many use-cases.
Versioned Mistral Large 2.1 model retained for integrations pinned to the 24.11 release.
Mistral Large 3 versioned model with long context and strong multimodal/coding capabilities.
Mistral's current flagship alias for high-quality reasoning, coding, and multimodal workloads.
Mistral's current medium-tier model, with a 256K-token context window and text, image, and document input.
Mistral's balanced mid-tier model for reasoning, coding, and multimodal workflows.
Open-weight Mistral Nemo model, useful for local or low-cost multilingual deployments.
Mistral's efficient small model alias for low-cost general-purpose and agentic workloads.
NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super, an open-weight hybrid MoE model for agentic reasoning, tool use, and long-context workloads.
Largest model in NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 family: a 550B mixture of experts with 55B active parameters and a 256K-token context window.
NVIDIA's latency-optimized Nemotron model, with a 256K-token context window at very low per-token cost.
OpenAI reasoning model. Extended thinking model optimized for complex reasoning, science, and coding. Charges for reasoning tokens.
Lightweight OpenAI reasoning model. Fast and cost-efficient reasoning for simpler tasks.

Meta-model that analyzes the prompt and routes each request to one of dozens of underlying models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and others), optimizing for output quality. Effective context window, pricing, knowledge cutoff, and tokenizer all track whichever model is selected; the response's `model` field reports the actual choice.
Groq-hosted Qwen3 32B open-weight model for reasoning, code, and multilingual work.
Fast, efficient Qwen variant. Optimized for high-volume applications.
Alibaba's flagship model. Strong multilingual and reasoning capabilities with large context support.

Qwen3.7-Plus is a cost-effective model in Alibaba's Qwen3.7 series. It supports text and image input with text output,
building on the series' text capabilities with a comprehensive upgrade to its vision-language abilities while retaining
full-stack, agent-level intelligence for coding, tool use, and productivity workflows. Its distinguishing trait is
multi-modal interactive hybrid agent capability: it can perceive real-world scenes, read screens and interact with GUIs,
generate code from visual references, and perform end-to-end navigation within mobile apps.

Open-weights release of the Qwen 3.8 Max architecture: a 2.4-trillion-parameter mixture of experts with
95B active parameters. Text-only, in contrast to the multimodal hosted Max endpoint.
Open-weights 27B dense model in the Qwen 3.8 family, with a 1M-token context window and text, image, and video input.

Fast, low-cost tier of the Qwen 3.8 family. Keeps the 1M-token context window and multimodal text, image,
and video input of Qwen 3.8 Max at a small fraction of the cost.

Alibaba's most capable Qwen model to date: a 2.4-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model accepting
text, image, and video input with text output, and reasoning enabled by default. Post-trained for coding and agentic
work including multi-step software projects, multi-tool orchestration, and long-horizon task execution. The 0902 snapshot
is the current release.
